primitives.name: Quasi-Arithmetic Pooling
primitives.verbatim_quote: To each such rule s we associate a corresponding method of aggregation, mapping expert forecasts and expert weights to a "consensus forecast," which we call quasi-arithmetic (QA) pooling with respect to s.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'p(j)': 'Probability of outcome j (dimensionless)', 's(x)': 'Scoring rule function (units depend on specific rule)', 's^{-1}(x)': 'Functional inverse of the scoring rule (inverse units)', 'w_i': 'Weight assigned to expert i (dimensionless)', 'p_i(j)': 'Probability forecast provided by expert i for outcome j (dimensionless)', 'm': 'Number of experts (dimensionless)'}
primitives.assumptions: Expert probabilities sum to one, weights are non-negative and sum to one, scoring rule is strictly increasing and continuous.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Singularity occurs when the argument of s lies outside its domain or when s is not invertible.

primitives.name: Logarithmic Pooling
primitives.verbatim_quote: These models all give you different answers: 10%, 25%, 70%.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'p(j)': 'Aggregated probability of outcome j (dimensionless)', 'p_i(j)': 'Probability forecast from expert i for outcome j (dimensionless)', 'w_i': 'weight assigned to expert i (dimensionless)', 'm': 'Number of experts (dimensionless)'}
primitives.assumptions: All expert probabilities are positive, weights are non-negative and sum to one.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Failure occurs when any expert assigns zero probability to the realized outcome, causing the product to vanish.

layer2.mapping: GSI - Bayes factor fusion of independent likelihoods. GSE - Multiplicative update rule for exponential families.

primitives.name: Max-Min Optimal Forecast Aggregation
primitives.verbatim_quote: • Given a scoring rule s used for payment, a forecaster agent who sub-contracts several experts, paying them in proportion to their weights, is best off aggregating the experts' reports using QA pooling with respect to s, meaning this strategy maximizes its worst-case profit (over the possible outcomes).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'A': 'Aggregation function (output is a probability distribution)', 's': 'Scoring rule (payoff per unit probability)', 'o': 'Realized outcome (category label)', 'E_s[Profit|o]': 'Expected profit conditioned on outcome o (monetary units)', 'max_min': 'Worst-case optimization criterion'}
primitives.assumptions: Forecaster acts competitively against nature, scoring rule is proper, expert payments are linear in weights.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Degeneracy happens when multiple outcomes tie for minimum expected profit, requiring additional tie-breaking criteria.

layer2.mapping: GSI - Robust Bayes posterior that minimizes maximum Kullback-Leibler divergence to any data-generating process. GSE - Value iteration for Markov decision processes with adversarial rewards.
layer2.telemetry: Max-min optimal aggregation coincides with QA pooling under the same scoring rule used for payment.

primitives.name: Online Gradient Descent for Expert Weights
primitives.verbatim_quote: As a consequence, online gradient descent can be used to learn appropriate expert weights from repeated experiments with low regret.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'w_i^{(t)}': 'Weight of expert i at time t (dimensionless)', 'R_t(w)': 'Cumulative loss at time t (scalar monetary units)', '\\eta': 'Learning rate (reciprocal of monetary units)', '\\Pi_{\\Delta}': 'Euclidean projection onto the probability simplex', '\\nabla R_t(w)': 'Gradient of loss with respect to weights (dimensionless)'}
primitives.assumptions: Loss functions are convex, gradients are bounded, weights lie in the probability simplex.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Instability arises when learning rate exceeds the reciprocal of the Lipschitz constant of the loss gradient.

layer2.mapping: GSI - Follow-the-regularized-leader algorithm with entropy regularization. GSE - Policy iteration with softmax exploration.
layer2.telemetry: Regret scales as O(sqrt(T)) for T rounds, matching information-theoretic lower bounds.

Starting from the max-min robustness property, we derive the necessary and sufficient condition for an aggregation operator to be optimal under adversarial losses. This leads to the QA form, where the link function is the derivative of the scoring rule's potential. Conversely, given a QA pool, we construct a scoring rule whose expected score is concave in expert weights, justifying the pool's optimality. The quadratic and logarithmic pools emerge as special cases corresponding to Euclidean geometry and information geometry, respectively. Failure modes occur when the scoring rule's curvature becomes singular or when the pooling operation maps probabilities outside the unit simplex.
